# Learned response-type coder

Trained on 328 clinician-adjudicated noun rows (15 target pictures), random forest on 42 features of the target/response pair plus the machine's own code. Accuracy is by leave-one-target-out cross-validation, so every row is predicted by a model that never saw its picture.

| | all 9 categories | five SP error types |
|---|---|---|
| rule-based machine code | 35% | 42% |
| learned, cross-validated | 51% (95% bootstrap 45% to 56%) | 68% |

The training rows are the ones the rule-based coder was unsure about, so these numbers describe performance on rows like those, which is where the model is applied; the machine's high-confidence rows (semantic with a WordNet relation, phonological nonwords within three edits, prefix fragments) are left as coded, because the clinician kept those categories when she saw them.
